title: Pinsker's inequality for the conditional law of Alice's special bit
statement:
Fix $n \ge 1$ and a deterministic two-party communication protocol $p$ for disjointness inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the transcript-and-side-information variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$. Write $\mu_z$ for the conditional law of Alice's bit $X_T$ at the special coordinate given that $Z = z$ — that is, the pushforward under the map $\omega \mapsto X_T(\omega)$ of the uniform measure on the sample space conditioned on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$ — and write $
u$ for the uniform law on a single bit. Then twice the squared total variation distance between $\mu_z$ and $
u$ is at most their Kullback–Leibler divergence,
\[
2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu_z, 
u)^2 \le D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu_z \,\|\, 
u).
\]
hypotheses_covered: length n is a positive natural number (n ≥ 1)
p is a deterministic protocol for disjointness inputs of length n
z is an achievable value of the Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T}) variable for p
